entry.title: Awesome Privacy Updates on Nov 05, 2026
entry.content:
VPNs / Apps

  • Free VPNs: a 2017 study of 283 Android VPN apps found 75% used trackers and 38% contained malware. Source

Password Managers / Useful Tools

  • LastPass: the UK fined it £1.2 million in 2025 over a 2022 breach that leaked customers' encrypted vaults. Source

Encryption / Useful Tools

  • BitLocker: your recovery key is uploaded to Microsoft by default, and Microsoft has handed such keys to the FBI. Source

Photo Editing and Management / Deezer alternative clients

  • Adobe Photoshop and Lightroom: its 2024 terms say Adobe may access your cloud content through both automated and manual review. Source

Video Editing / Deezer alternative clients

  • Adobe Premiere Pro: its terms allow automated scanning of your Creative Cloud files and human review of flagged ones. Source

Ebooks / Plugins for Minecraft

  • Amazon Kindle: in 2009 Amazon remotely deleted copies of 1984 that people had bought from their Kindles. Source

Android Debloat Tools / Plugins for Minecraft

  • ADB AppControl: its terms let it send your PC's IP, hardware details and the apps you remove to a remote server. Source

Android Gallery / Plugins for Minecraft

  • Google Photos: scans your photos, and in 2022 its scan got a father investigated by police over photos taken for a doctor. Source

Home Assistants / Other OS

  • Siri: in 2025 Apple settled claims that Siri recorded private conversations without consent for $95 million. Source

Payments / Apps and services

  • Visa / Mastercard: your card purchases feed Mastercard audience segments, like affluent shoppers, sold on data marketplaces. Source

Legend / Apps and services

  • ⚠️ closed server: the server code isn't public.
  • ⚠️ account required: an account is needed to use it.

entry.title: Awesome Privacy Updates on Nov 04, 2026
entry.content:
Video and Audio Conferencing / Desktop

  • WhatsApp: in 2021 Ireland fined it €225 million for not properly explaining what data it shares with Facebook. ToS;DR · Source
  • Zoom: paid $85 million in 2021 to settle claims it shared user data with Facebook, Google and LinkedIn. ToS;DR · Source
  • BigBlueButton - Self-hosted web conferencing built for online classes, with whiteboard, breakout rooms and recordings. ⚠️ website trackers self-host · LGPL-3.0
  • Briefing - Group video chat in the browser over direct WebRTC connections, with no account. self-host · AGPL-3.0
  • Chitchatter - Serverless, ephemeral peer-to-peer chat with audio, video, screen and file sharing. GPL-2.0
  • Jami - Peer-to-peer audio and video calls and chat with no central servers or account needed. GPL-3.0 · F-Droid
  • Jitsi Meet - Video conferencing you can self-host; the official instance requires you to log in. self-host · Apache-2.0 · F-Droid (Play Store version has trackers)
  • MiroTalk P2P - Browser-based peer-to-peer video calls up to 4K, with nothing to install. AGPL-3.0
  • Mumble - Low-latency voice chat with encrypted connections, on servers you can run yourself. self-host

Instant Messaging

  • Facebook Messenger: chats have been encrypted since 2023, but Meta still sees who you message, when, and who your contacts are. ToS;DR · Exodus · Source

Instagram / Desktop

  • Instagram: Ireland fined Meta €405 million in 2022 for exposing children's emails and phone numbers on Instagram. ToS;DR · Source
  • Pixelfed - Federated photo sharing with posts, stories and a chronological feed, without ads. ActivityPub · AGPL-3.0

Location Tracking / Apps and services

  • Google Find Hub (formerly Find My Device): reports your devices' locations to Google. ToS;DR

Teamworking Tools / Desktop

  • Wire - End-to-end encrypted messaging, calls and file sharing for teams, with public and audited code for both the apps and the server. ⚠️ website trackers AGPL-3.0 · F-Droid (Play Store version has trackers)
  • Discord: a 2025 breach at a support vendor exposed government ID photos of about 70,000 users. ToS;DR · Source
  • Slack: your messages feed its recommendation models unless a workspace owner emails Slack to opt out. ToS;DR · Source
  • Rocket.Chat - Self-hosted team chat with end-to-end encrypted rooms and federation. ⚠️ website trackers self-host
  • Twake Chat - Workplace chat built on Matrix, part of Linagora's Twake Workplace suite. AGPL-3.0

Maps and Navigation / Apps and services

  • Bing Maps: under Microsoft's very poorly rated privacy policy. ToS;DR
  • Yandex Maps: 11 trackers in its Android app, from a company bound by Russian surveillance law. Exodus
  • Sygic: 8 trackers in its Android app. Exodus
  • OpenStreetMap (OSM) - Collaborative world map built by volunteers, and the open data behind most apps in this section. GPL-2.0
    • OsmAnd - Offline maps and navigation built on OpenStreetMap, with a large set of features. ⚠️ telemetry opt-out Android · iOS · F-Droid
  • Pure Maps - Maps and navigation for Linux phones, Sailfish OS and desktop, fully offline with OSM Scout Server. Linux · GPL-3.0

Search Engines / Useful Tools

  • Yahoo!: a 2013 breach hit all 3 billion Yahoo accounts, which Yahoo admitted only in 2017. ToS;DR · Source
  • Yandex: in 2025 researchers found its Android apps, Yandex Search among them, secretly linked browsing to device IDs. ToS;DR · Source
  • Brave Search - Search engine with its own independent index, from the makers of Brave.
  • DuckDuckGo - Search engine that doesn't build a profile on you, with results drawn largely from Bing.
  • Marginalia - Independent search engine with its own crawler and index that favors text-heavy, non-commercial pages. self-host
  • Mojeek - UK search engine with its own crawler and index and a no-tracking policy.
  • Qwant - French search engine, hosted in the EU, that doesn't track your searches.
  • SearXNG - Metasearch engine that queries other search services for you; use a public instance or host your own. self-host · AGPL-3.0
  • YaCy - Peer-to-peer search engine where every user runs a node and shares the index.

Third-party

  • Proton Mail - Email from Switzerland, end-to-end encrypted between Proton users and with PGP, and stored encrypted otherwise, where a court order can still force it to log your IP (2021 case). GPL-3.0

Self-hosted

  • Docker Mailserver - Complete mail server (SMTP, IMAP, antispam, antivirus) in a single Docker container, configured with files. self-host · MIT
  • Mail-in-a-box - Turns a fresh Ubuntu server into a complete mail server with one setup script. self-host · CC0-1.0
  • Mailcow: dockerized - Docker-based mail server suite with a web admin panel, webmail and groupware. self-host · GPL-3.0
  • Mox - Self-contained mail server in a single binary, built to need little maintenance. self-host · MIT

Clients / Android / iOS

  • FairEmail - Full-featured email app that blocks tracking images and keeps everything on your device. Android · GPL-3.0 · F-Droid
  • Thunderbird for Android - Mozilla's email app for Android, built on K-9 Mail, which still ships from the same code. Android · Apache-2.0 · F-Droid

Clients / Desktop

  • NeoMutt - Terminal email client with built-in PGP/GPG support, a maintained fork of Mutt. Linux · macOS · CLI · GPL-2.0

Email Alias Services (Anonymous Forwarding) / Desktop

  • addy.io - Email alias and forwarding service you can host yourself, formerly AnonAddy. self-host · AGPL-3.0
  • SimpleLogin - Email alias service you can host yourself, owned by Proton. self-host · AGPL-3.0

Alternative clients/modifications of Discord / Desktop

  • Aliucord (⭐4.9k) - Mod for the Android Discord app that disables Discord's tracking (⭐4.9k). Android · OSL-3.0
  • BetterDiscord - Discord client mod; add the DoNotTrack plugin to block trackers. Apache-2.0
  • Legcord - Lightweight Discord client that blocks Discord's known trackers by default, formerly ArmCord. OSL-3.0
  • OpenAsar - Drop-in replacement for part of the Discord desktop app, with a No Tracking (⭐3k) option that turns off crash and error reporting. AGPL-3.0
  • Replugged - Discord client mod that continues the discontinued Powercord. MIT
  • Vencord - Discord client mod with plugins, including one that blocks Discord's tracking. GPL-3.0
  • Vesktop - Desktop Discord client with Vencord built in, which blocks Discord's telemetry. GPL-3.0
  • WebCord (⭐2.5k) - Discord client that loads the web app in Electron instead of using the Discord API, with extra privacy settings. MIT

Blogging platforms (Medium) / Desktop

  • Medium: the site carries trackers, under a poorly rated privacy policy. ToS;DR
  • Plume - Federated blogging engine where readers can follow and comment from any ActivityPub account. 💀 inactive ActivityPub
  • WriteFreely - Minimal, distraction-free blogging platform that can federate posts over ActivityPub. ActivityPub · AGPL-3.0

YouTube / Desktop

  • YouTube: Google paid a record $170 million in 2019 for collecting children's data on YouTube without parental consent. ToS;DR · Source
  • PeerTube - Federated video hosting where anyone can run an instance and follow channels across others. ActivityPub · AGPL-3.0

YouTube / Frontends

  • Invidious - YouTube frontend with no ads or Google scripts and subscriptions without an account; see the public instances. AGPL-3.0
  • youtube-local (⭐779) - YouTube client that runs on your computer and opens in the browser, with local subscriptions and optional routing through Tor. Desktop · AGPL-3.0

YouTube / Apps

  • FreeTube - Desktop YouTube app that keeps subscriptions, playlists and history on your computer, without Google's cookies or scripts. Desktop · AGPL-3.0
  • LibreTube - Android YouTube app that fetches videos through Piped instead of Google's servers. Android · GPL-3.0 · F-Droid
  • NewPipe - Lightweight Android YouTube app with background play and downloads, no Google services or account needed. Android · GPL-3.0 · F-Droid
  • SkyTube (⭐2.8k) - Android YouTube app with local subscriptions, downloads and a channel and video blocker. Android · GPL-3.0 · F-Droid
  • Yattee (⭐3.8k) - Native YouTube player for iPhone, iPad, Apple TV and Mac that works through Invidious or Piped. iOS · macOS · AGPL-3.0

Twitter / Apps

  • Twitter (X): paid $150 million in 2022 for using phone numbers given for account security to target ads. ToS;DR · Source

Twitter / Decentralized

  • Mastodon - Federated microblogging, the largest network in the fediverse. ActivityPub · AGPL-3.0 · F-Droid
    • Mastodon Apps - Official directory of Mastodon apps for Android, iOS, web and desktop.
  • Pleroma - Lightweight federated social network server. ActivityPub
    • Soapbox - Web frontend for Pleroma focused on custom branding and ease of use.

Twitter / Frontends

  • Nitter (⭐14k) - Twitter frontend without JavaScript or ads that proxies every request; see the instances list (⭐14k). 💀 inactive AGPL-3.0
  • Squawker (⭐1.5k) - Android Twitter client with no account, tracking or ads, keeping subscriptions on the device; the maintained fork of Fritter. Android · MIT · F-Droid

Reddit / Frontends

  • Reddit: sold Google the right to train AI on users' posts in a 2024 deal valued at about $60 million. ToS;DR · Source

Reddit / Alternatives

  • Lemmy - Federated link aggregator and discussion forum, organized into communities like subreddits. ActivityPub · AGPL-3.0
  • Mbin - Federated link aggregator with microblogging, the community-run continuation of kbin. ActivityPub · AGPL-3.0

Streaming Platforms (Twitch) / Apps and frontends

  • Twitch: a 2021 breach leaked 125GB of its data, including source code and three years of creator payouts. ToS;DR · Source
  • Owncast - Self-hosted live streaming server with built-in chat, so you own the stream and your viewers' data. self-host · MIT

Streaming Platforms (Twitch) / Apps

  • Twire (⭐1.3k) - Android Twitch client with built-in ad blocking, VODs with chat replay, and optional login. Android · GPL-3.0 · F-Droid

Imgur / Apps

  • Imgur: a 2014 hack stole about 1.7 million email addresses and passwords, which it only learned of in 2017. ToS;DR · Exodus · Source
  • rimgo - Read-only Imgur frontend that works without JavaScript; see the instances.

IMDb / Apps

  • IMDb: owned by Amazon, with 8 trackers in its Android app. ToS;DR · Exodus
  • libremdb (⭐441) - IMDb frontend without ads or tracking that proxies images and video through the instance. self-host · AGPL-3.0

Fandom / Apps

  • Fandom: wikis loaded with ads and autoplaying video, and 8 trackers in the app. ToS;DR · Exodus

Commenting Engines / Apps

  • Disqus: tracked visitors across sites for ad profiling without consent, Norway's regulator said in 2021. ToS;DR · Source
  • Isso - Lightweight self-hosted comment server, meant as a drop-in replacement for Disqus. self-host · MIT

Translation / Apps

  • DeepL: the free version may train on your texts, and its terms forbid entering any personal data. ToS;DR · Source

Text translation / Apps

  • LibreTranslate - Self-hosted machine translation API and web app with no ties to proprietary services. self-host · AGPL-3.0

Alternative Google Translate frontends / Apps

  • Mozhi - Frontend that proxies Google Translate, DeepL, Yandex and other engines behind one interface. self-host
  • SimplyTranslate - Frontend that proxies your requests to Google Translate and other engines. self-host

RSS Readers / Apps

  • Capy Reader (⭐1.4k) - Small RSS reader, local or synced with Miniflux and FreshRSS. Android · GPL-3.0 · F-Droid (Play Store version has trackers)
  • Feeder (⭐3.1k) - RSS reader that fetches feeds directly on your device, with no account. Android · GPL-3.0
  • Fluent Reader (⭐9.8k) - Desktop RSS reader that keeps your feeds locally, with optional sync to self-hosted services. Linux · Windows · macOS · BSD-3-Clause
  • FreshRSS - Self-hosted feed aggregator with a web interface, multi-user support and an API for mobile apps. self-host · AGPL-3.0
  • Miniflux - Minimalist self-hosted feed reader with no tracking, written in Go. self-host · Apache-2.0
  • NetNewsWire - RSS reader for Mac, iPhone and iPad that works locally or syncs with self-hosted services. macOS · iOS · MIT
  • Newsboat - RSS reader for the terminal, configured with plain text files. Linux · macOS · CLI · MIT
  • NewsFlash - RSS reader for Linux that works locally or with self-hosted services such as Miniflux and FreshRSS. Linux · GPL-3.0
  • Read You (⭐7.6k) - Material You RSS reader, local or synced with self-hosted services. Android · GPL-3.0

VPNs / Apps

  • SPN - Paid add-on to the Portmaster firewall that routes each app's connections over separate multi-hop paths. Linux · Windows · GPL-3.0

Web Browser / Apps

  • Opera: 6 trackers in its Android app, and owned by a Chinese consortium since 2016. Exodus · Source

Android / iOS / Apps

  • Cromite (⭐8.5k) - Chromium fork, successor to Bromite, with built-in ad blocking and anti-fingerprinting measures. Android · Linux · Windows · GPL-3.0
  • Firefox - Mozilla's browser, with its own engine on Android and Enhanced Tracking Protection on by default. ⚠️ website trackers ⚠️ telemetry opt-out
    • IronFox - Hardened Firefox for Android with proprietary blobs removed, a fork of the discontinued Mull. Android
  • Privacy Browser - Browser that keeps JavaScript, cookies and other tracking features off until you allow them per site. Android
  • Vanadium - Hardened Chromium from the GrapheneOS project, and the default browser on GrapheneOS. Android

Browser Addons / Anti-tracking

  • LibRedirect - Redirects YouTube, Reddit, Google Maps and other sites to privacy-friendly front ends, successor to Privacy Redirect. Browser · GPL-3.0
    • Predirect (⭐279) - Similar extension built on Manifest V3 with minimal permissions, for Chromium browsers that no longer run older extensions. Browser · GPL-3.0

Browser Addons / Useful Tools

  • SingleFile (⭐23k) - Saves a complete web page as a single HTML file you can open offline. Browser · AGPL-3.0

Domains & Hosting / Useful Tools

  • OrangeWebsite - Icelandic web host focused on free speech, with anonymous signup and cryptocurrency or cash payment. ⚠️ website trackers

Link Shorteners / Useful Tools

  • Bitly: built to track every click for marketing analytics. ToS;DR
  • Kutt - Shortener with custom domains and password-protected links that you can host yourself. self-host · MIT
  • YOURLS - Self-hosted shortener written in PHP, with its own click stats and a plugin system. self-host · MIT

Captchas / Useful Tools

  • hCaptcha: its privacy policy says it supplies the answers visitors give to its puzzles as AI training data. ToS;DR · Source
  • ALTCHA - Self-hosted proof-of-work captcha with no cookies or tracking. self-host · MIT
  • mCaptcha - Proof-of-work captcha that rate-limits bots by making each request cost some computation. self-host · AGPL-3.0
  • Private Captcha - EU-made proof-of-work captcha, as a hosted service or on your own server. ⚠️ source-available self-host

2FA / Useful Tools

  • Authy: needs your phone number, and a 2024 leak exposed 33 million of them. Source
  • Microsoft Authenticator: 5 trackers in its Android app, and no way to export your tokens to another app. Exodus
  • 2FAS Auth - Authenticator whose browser extension asks your phone for a code and fills it in, no account needed. GPL-3.0
  • Aegis - Encrypted token vault that imports from most other authenticators and exports in plain or encrypted form. Android · GPL-3.0 · F-Droid
  • ente Auth - Authenticator with end-to-end encrypted sync between your devices, from the makers of ente Photos. ⚠️ website trackers AGPL-3.0
  • FreeOTPPlus (⭐750) - Fork of FreeOTP with backups, search and dark mode. Android · Apache-2.0 · F-Droid
  • Stratum (⭐4.6k) - Authenticator with Wear OS support and encrypted backups. Android · GPL-3.0

Password Managers / Useful Tools

  • KeePassXC - Offline password manager that keeps your vault in an encrypted file you control, with no account or sync service. Linux · macOS · Windows
    • KeePassDX - KeePass-compatible password manager for Android. Android · GPL-3.0 · F-Droid
    • Strongbox - KeePass-compatible password manager for iPhone, iPad and Mac. iOS · macOS · AGPL-3.0

Encryption / Useful Tools

  • age - Simple, modern file encryption with small keys and nothing to configure. CLI · BSD-3-Clause
  • Cryptomator - Encrypts files on your device before they reach any cloud storage provider. GPL-3.0 · F-Droid
  • Shufflecake - Hidden encrypted volumes for Linux with plausible deniability, so nobody can prove the hidden data exists. Linux
  • Stegcloak - Hides password-protected secrets inside ordinary text using invisible characters. ⚠️ website trackers 💀 inactive
  • Tomb - Creates and manages encrypted folders on Linux, built on standard LUKS. Linux · CLI · GPL-3.0
  • VeraCrypt - Encrypts whole disks, partitions or file containers, with support for hidden volumes. Linux · macOS · Windows

Pastebin and Secret Sharing / Useful Tools

  • Deleto - Shares passwords and other secrets with client-side encryption and automatic self-destruction.

Android / Useful Tools

  • NetGuard - Blocks internet access per app, no root needed. Android · GPL-3.0 · F-Droid
  • Orbot - Routes app traffic through Tor, for all apps or only the ones you choose. Made by the Guardian Project. Android
  • Plexus - Community database of which apps work on de-Googled Android. Android · F-Droid
  • RethinkDNS + Firewall (⭐5.8k) - Firewall and encrypted DNS client in one, no root needed. Android · Apache-2.0 · F-Droid (Play Store version has trackers)
  • εxodus - Shows which trackers and permissions an Android app contains, before you install it. AGPL-3.0
    • ClassyShark3xodus - Checks the apps on your phone for known trackers, using the εxodus database. Android · F-Droid

Cloud Storage / Useful Tools

  • Dropbox: a 2012 breach exposed 68 million users' emails and passwords, which Dropbox only confirmed in 2016. ToS;DR · Exodus · Source
  • Sync-in - Self-hosted file storage, sharing and sync with WebDAV, desktop clients and online document editing. self-host · AGPL-3.0

File Management and Sharing / Useful Tools

  • WeTransfer: in 2025 it changed its terms to license your uploaded files for machine learning, then backed down. ToS;DR · Source
  • Blaze - Peer-to-peer file sharing in the browser, between two or more devices at once. ⚠️ website trackers 💀 inactive MIT
  • Croc (⭐41k) - Sends files between two computers with end-to-end encryption, using a short code phrase. CLI · MIT
  • Gokapi (⭐2.9k) - Lightweight self-hosted alternative to Firefox Send, where only you can upload and links expire. self-host · AGPL-3.0
  • Localsend - Shares files with nearby devices over your local network, with no internet connection or account needed. Apache-2.0 · F-Droid
  • Lufi - File sharing server that encrypts uploads in your browser, so the server never sees the contents. self-host
  • Magic Wormhole (⭐23k) - Sends files from one computer to another with end-to-end encryption, using a short one-time code. CLI · MIT
  • OnionShare (⭐7.2k) - Shares files, hosts websites and runs chat rooms over Tor onion services, anonymously and without a third-party server.
  • PairDrop (⭐12k) - Snapdrop fork that shares files in the browser on your local network, and with paired devices beyond it. fork · GPL-3.0
  • Paperless-ngx (⭐48k) - Self-hosted document manager that scans, indexes and archives your paperwork on your own server. self-host · GPL-3.0
  • QRcp (⭐11k) - Transfers files over Wi-Fi from your computer to your phone by scanning a QR code in the terminal. CLI · MIT
  • scrt.link - End-to-end encrypted file transfer of up to 100 GB, stored in Switzerland for up to 30 days. MIT
  • Send - Fork of Firefox Send that encrypts files in the browser and expires links after a set time or number of downloads. self-host · fork
  • Snapdrop - Local file sharing in the browser, inspired by Apple's AirDrop. self-host · GPL-3.0
  • Winden - Magic Wormhole in the browser, for end-to-end encrypted transfers without installing anything. MIT

Download Manager / Useful Tools

  • Motrix - Full-featured download manager for HTTP, FTP, BitTorrent and magnet links. Desktop
  • Persepolis Download Manager - Graphical front end for aria2 with download scheduling and video grabbing. Desktop · GPL-3.0
  • Xtreme Download Manager - Download accelerator that resumes broken downloads and saves streaming video from many sites. ⚠️ website trackers Desktop · GPL-3.0

Bookmarking / Useful Tools

  • Evernote Web Clipper: in 2016 Evernote changed its policy to let staff read users' notes, until users pushed back. ToS;DR · Source
  • Karakeep - Self-hosted app for saving links, notes and images, with full-text search and optional AI tagging, formerly Hoarder. self-host · AGPL-3.0

Notes and Tasks / Useful Tools

  • Notion: no end-to-end encryption, so Notion can read everything in your workspace. ToS;DR
  • Lockbook - End-to-end encrypted notebook for notes, documents and drawings, as an Evernote alternative. Unlicense
  • OpenHabitTracker - Habit, task and note tracker that keeps your data on the device, or syncs to a server you run yourself. ⚠️ website trackers
  • Super Productivity - To-do list and time tracker that keeps data local with no account, with optional sync over WebDAV or Dropbox. MIT
  • Tasks.org - To-do and task manager that works offline, with CalDAV sync. ⚠️ website trackers Android · GPL-3.0 · F-Droid (Play Store version has trackers)

Office / Useful Tools

  • Collabora Office - LibreOffice-based office suite for desktop and mobile, from the team behind Collabora Online.
  • CryptPad - Collaborative documents, spreadsheets and more, end-to-end encrypted so the server can't read them. self-host · AGPL-3.0

PDF Tools / Useful Tools

  • iLovePDF: uploads your documents to its servers, and the Android app has 7 trackers. ToS;DR · Exodus
  • Smallpdf: uploads your documents to its servers, and the Android app has 3 trackers. ToS;DR · Exodus
  • BentoPDF - Browser-based PDF toolkit to merge, split, compress, sign and redact, with files processed on your device. Web · self-host · AGPL-3.0

Calendar / Useful Tools

  • Etar (⭐2.6k) - Calendar app that works with any CalDAV server through a sync adapter. Android · GPL-3.0 · F-Droid
  • Fossify Calendar (⭐2.3k) - Offline calendar with widgets and no ads, which can also sync with your device's CalDAV accounts. Android · GPL-3.0 · F-Droid
  • KashCal (⭐468) - Offline-first calendar with built-in iCloud and CalDAV sync, full-text search and widgets. Android · F-Droid
  • Nextcloud Calendar - Calendar app for your Nextcloud server, with CalDAV sync to your other devices. self-host · AGPL-3.0
  • Proton Calendar - End-to-end encrypted calendar from the makers of Proton Mail.

Media Streaming Platforms / Useful Tools

  • Netflix: in 2024 Dutch regulators fined Netflix €4.75 million for not telling users what it does with their data. ToS;DR · Source
  • Amazon Prime Video: 3 trackers in its Android app, under a poorly rated privacy policy. ToS;DR · Exodus
  • Disney Plus: in 2026 Disney paid California $2.75 million for sharing streaming viewers' data after they had opted out. ToS;DR · Source
  • SoundCloud: a 2025 breach exposed the email addresses of about 28 million users, a fifth of its community. ToS;DR · Exodus · Source

Podcasts / Deezer alternative clients

  • Spotify: in 2023 Sweden fined Spotify 58 million kronor for not clearly explaining how it uses your data. ToS;DR · Exodus · Source
  • Funkwhale - Federated platform for hosting, sharing and listening to podcasts and music. self-host · ActivityPub
  • iVoox: 13 trackers in its Android app, and more on its website. Exodus
  • Deezer: a partner leaked a 2019 backup of 229 million users' names, birth dates, IPs and locations, published in 2022. Exodus · Source
  • AntennaPod - Podcast player that subscribes to any RSS feed, with no account needed. Android · GPL-3.0 · F-Droid

Audio / Useful Tools

  • Ampache - Web-based server for streaming your own music and video collection. self-host · AGPL-3.0
  • Koel - Personal music streaming server with a web player. self-host · MIT
  • mucke (⭐268) - Player for local music files with custom playback rules. Android · GPL-3.0 · F-Droid
  • Navidrome - Lightweight music server for your own collection, compatible with Subsonic apps. ⚠️ website trackers self-host · GPL-3.0
  • Nuclear - Desktop music player that streams from free sources, with no account. Linux · macOS · Windows · AGPL-3.0

Audio / Spotify alternative clients

  • ncspot (⭐6.8k) - Terminal Spotify client written in Rust, inspired by ncmpc. Needs Spotify Premium. CLI · BSD-2-Clause
  • psst (⭐9.5k) - Fast Spotify client with a native GUI written in Rust. Needs Spotify Premium. Linux · macOS · Windows · MIT
  • Spotube - Plugin-based music player that can load your Spotify playlists and stream the audio from other sources, no Premium needed. AGPL-3.0

Audio / YouTube Music alternative clients

  • SimpMusic - YouTube Music client with no ads and SponsorBlock built in, successor to the discontinued ViMusic and RiMusic. ⚠️ website trackers Android · Desktop · GPL-3.0 · F-Droid

Home Assistants / Other OS

  • Alexa: the FTC fined Amazon $25 million in 2023 for keeping children's Alexa voice recordings indefinitely. ToS;DR · Source
  • OpenVoiceOS - Voice assistant you run on your own hardware, a community successor to Mycroft. Apache-2.0

Music Recognition / Deezer alternative clients

  • Shazam: owned by Apple, and its Android app carries Google's analytics trackers. Exodus
  • SoundHound: 11 trackers in its Android app. Exodus
  • Musixmatch: 8 trackers in its Android app. Exodus

Android Gallery / Plugins for Minecraft

  • Amazon Photos: its privacy notice says Amazon uses the images you store with it to improve its services. Source
  • Fossify Gallery - Photo and video gallery with no ads, a fork of Simple Gallery. Android · GPL-3.0 · F-Droid

Self-hosted / Deezer alternative clients

  • Immich - Self-hosted photo and video backup straight from your phone, the closest match to Google Photos. self-host · AGPL-3.0 · F-Droid
  • PhotoPrism - Self-hosted photo library with automatic tagging and face recognition that runs on your own server. self-host
  • PiGallery2 - Self-hosted, directory-first photo gallery website. self-host · MIT

Third-party / Deezer alternative clients

Privacy vs Security vs Anonymity / Apps and services

  • Anonymity means your actions can't be traced back to you. Someone may see what is done, but not who did it.

  • ⚠️ website trackers: the project's website loads third-party trackers. That says nothing about the app itself.
  • ⚠️ telemetry opt-out: the app sends usage data by default, but a setting turns it off.
